items.front: Order in which Central Asian powers entered NW India after the Mauryas?
items.back: Indo-Greeks → Shakas → Parthians → Kushanas (Kushanas came last and displaced the Shakas & Parthians).
items.examPoint: Central Asian contacts & sequence (Indo-Greeks → Shakas → Parthians → Kushanas)

items.front: Who are the Shakas, and who displaced them into India?
items.back: The Shakas = Scythians, nomads of Central Asia; pushed towards India by the Yuezhi (after wars with the Chinese).
items.examPoint: Shakas (Scythians) — origin, displacement by Yuezhi, spread

items.front: Shaka branch → capital: Punjab, Mathura, Western India?
items.back: Punjab — Maues (Taxila); Mathura — Azilises; Gujarat/W. India — Rudradaman I (Ujjain). Afghanistan branch: Vonones/Spalirises.
items.examPoint: Five branches of the Shakas & their capitals

items.back: First major Shaka king; ruled Punjab/Gandhara from Taxila; coins with Greek deities (Zeus, Athena); backed Buddhism.

items.front: Greatest Shaka ruler and his achievements?
items.back: Rudradaman I (c.130–150 CE): defeated the Satavahanas; held Gujarat/Sindh/Kutch/Malwa; first long Sanskrit inscription.
items.examPoint: Rudradaman I — greatest Shaka, conquests, defeat of Satavahanas

items.front: Junagadh (Girnar) inscription of Rudradaman — language & script?
items.back: First LONG inscription in chaste Sanskrit, written in Brahmi script (NOT Kharoshti); records the Sudarshana Lake repair.

items.front: Junagadh rock — which THREE rulers inscribed on it?
items.back: Ashoka (14 Major Rock Edicts) + Rudradaman I (~150 CE) + Skandagupta (~455 CE, another Sudarshana repair).
items.examPoint: Junagadh rock — three rulers (Ashoka, Rudradaman, Skandagupta) & Brahmi script

items.front: Sudarshana Lake — original builder and how Rudradaman repaired it?
items.back: Built under Chandragupta Maurya (gov. Pushyagupta); Rudradaman repaired it WITHOUT forced labour (vishti)/new taxes via governor Suvishakha.
items.examPoint: Sudarshana Lake details — Mauryan origin, no forced labour, governor Suvishakha

items.front: Who founded the Western Kshatrapas, and where?
items.back: Chastana — capital Ujjain; grandfather-line to Rudradaman I, the dynasty's greatest ruler.
items.examPoint: Chastana & the Western Kshatrapas at Ujjain

items.front: Shaka administrative titles, top to junior?
items.back: Mahasenapati (supreme commander) · Satrap (provincial military governor) · Kshatrapa (junior satrap) · Raja (regional king).

items.front: Saka era vs Vikram Samvat — years?
items.back: Saka era = 78 CE (India's national/Saka Samvat calendar). Vikram Samvat = 58 BCE. Watch the BCE/CE reversal.
items.examPoint: Saka era (78 CE) vs Vikram Samvat (58 BCE) & decline of the Shakas

items.front: Who took the title 'Vikramaditya'/'Sakari' by beating the Western Kshatrapas?
items.back: Gupta emperor Chandragupta II (c. 409 CE) — 'Sakari' = destroyer of the Shakas; ended Shaka rule in western India.
items.examPoint: Vikramaditya title & Chandragupta II 'Sakari'; Gandhara Greco-Roman art

items.front: How does the Manusmriti classify the Shakas & Parthians?
items.back: As 'fallen Kshatriyas' — reflecting their gradual absorption into the warrior varna (Rudradaman–Satavahana marriage alliance).

items.front: Gondophernes — dynasty, capital, religious link, dating inscription?
items.back: Most prominent Parthian (Pahlava); capital Taxila; linked to St Thomas (early Christianity); Takht-i-Bahi inscription = 45 CE.
items.examPoint: Gondophernes — St Thomas, Buddhism, Takht-i-Bahi inscription (45 CE)

items.front: What was the Gandhara school of sculpture influenced by?
items.back: Greco-Roman (Hellenistic) style — realistic drapery, wavy hair, muscular Buddhas; flourished under Shaka-Parthian & Kushana rule.
items.examPoint: Vikramaditya title & Chandragupta II 'Sakari'; Gandhara Greco-Roman art
